note: Banks in Guam are numbered within the United States' routing number system: the American Bankers Association's Routing Number Policy and Procedures (the Routing Number Administrative Board's policy, revised 9/20, read 2026-10-30 on aba.com) defines a Federal Reserve District as one of the twelve areas assigned to a Federal Reserve Bank main office and says all of the United States and its territories fall into one of these twelve districts, whose routing symbols (01-12) begin a bank's routing number; the FDIC's BankFind data (read 2026-10-30) lists 17 FDIC-insured bank offices in Guam (Bank of Guam, Bank of Hawaii, BankPacific, Finance Factors and First Hawaiian Bank); and Bank of Guam, the territory's own bank, gives its routing number, 121405115, on its own page (read 2026-10-30), a number that passes the United States' check digit. So an account there is numbered as one in the United States: a routing number and an account number of one to seventeen characters. (Wave 8's file, held for want of the account's length, gave the routing number alone; the United States' own form now takes the account.)

sources.title: American Bankers Association, Routing Number Policy and Procedures (revised 9/20)
sources.said: Federal Reserve District One of the twelve geographic areas assigned to a Federal Reserve Bank main office. All of the United States and its territories fall into one of these twelve districts.
